title: Duplicate source claims are not independent corroboration
observation: BEAN evidence ranker documents origin grouping and separation of independently verified outcomes from repeated copies.
how_learned: Engineering tests and explicit provenance rules prompted an origin-deduplication design; no claim of spontaneous model learning.
what_changed: Source copies from the same declared origin count once for the evidence ranker.
validated_outcome: Repository documentation describes implementation and regression checks; external authentication still absent.
transfer_test: Test spoofed identities, copied sources, correlated attestations and genuine independent signed witnesses.
limitations: User-supplied origin and verification fields can be false.

title: Preserve competing hypotheses when evidence conflicts
observation: DualStateReasoner supports unknown, insufficient, contested and context-required states; evidence is append-only.
how_learned: Ambiguity and contradictory evidence were represented explicitly in a context-scoped state machine.
what_changed: BEAN Core records both hypotheses without forcing a binary verdict on conflict.
actual_learning_mechanism: deterministic evidence-routing rule, not model-weight learning
validated_outcome: Documented API and targeted tests; not calibrated as a probability of truth.
transfer_test: Held-out ambiguous physics, safety and manufacturing cases with independent source checks.
limitations: Separate origin labels do not guarantee independent observations.

title: A backup file is not proof of recoverable memory
observation: A backup procedure that created a file but did not verify restore completeness was identified and replaced with a restore-copy drill.
how_learned: Defect review identified missing integrity, replay, collision and partial-publication checks; regression testing exercised the revised procedure.
what_changed: Backup now produces SHA256 receipts, checks SQLite consistency and exercises a disposable restore.
actual_learning_mechanism: engineer-directed code revision following test evidence
validated_outcome: Code-level restore validation documented; no power-loss or long-duration field-test proof.
transfer_test: Disk-full fault injection, unclean shutdown, off-host restores and signed-receipt validation.
limitations: Source authenticity and operational disaster recovery remain unproven.

title: Synthetic metric gains can hide regressions
observation: Lab003 reported improved change recall in one synthetic condition, while other conditions regressed. Lab004 included a case where fresh-start memory still performed better on mean reward.
how_learned: Ablation and varied synthetic trials exposed that improvement was metric- and condition-dependent.
what_changed: Research documentation retains non-winning baselines and caveats; no generalization claim is promoted.
actual_learning_mechanism: researcher interpretation of held-out synthetic outputs; not neural training
validated_outcome: Synthetic-only mixed evidence; no general agent advantage established.
transfer_test: Preregister varied sources and distributions, measure false positives, cost, all target metrics and real-world holdouts.
limitations: Synthetic environments can encode benchmark-specific advantages.

title: A persisted lesson is not proof that the agent learned
observation: Lab023 live provider attempt was rate-limited. Hosted local model pilot stored and reopened three reflections, but missing candidate and model-identity receipts made the cold-versus-memory comparison inconclusive.
how_learned: A causal cold-memory comparison and independent judges exposed measurement and provider-identity weaknesses.
what_changed: Study correctly reports inconclusive rather than granting a learning-success claim; add complete served-model identity receipts.
actual_learning_mechanism: prompt memory persistence and controlled evaluation proposal; no model-weight update
transfer_test: Use same served model with per-request IDs, equal budgets, blind unseen tasks, placebo memory, multiple seeds and full candidate accounting.
limitations: Inadequate paired model provenance and missing candidates prevent attribution.

title: PEMDAS two-pass attention may enable mnemonic recovery
observation: Originator reported near-instant whole-screen survey, nouns and verbs as initial scene anchors and faster detailed second reading.
how_learned: Hypothesis elicited from a human reading technique, not independently validated by an agent.
what_changed: Research proposal and mnemonic-cued recovery test plan were documented; no validated runtime change.
validated_outcome: Unknown. Requires reproducible matched real-agent measurements.
transfer_test: Run baseline first, then two isolated same-model agents over five cutoff windows; test uncued/cued recall, negation, hallucinations and total latency.
limitations: No real LLM experiment or causal result established from the available connected runtime.

title: Memory quality requires provenance and version history, not just quantity
observation: Letta documents versioned MemFS memory edits; SWE-agent documents full trajectories and rerunnable configuration files. BEAN has durable journal and evidence hashes but lacks a single cross-component learning-change receipt contract.
how_learned: Review of peer implementation patterns against BEAN memory and evidence documentation.
what_changed: This lesson registry begins source-linked documentation; it does not automatically update model policy or weights.
validated_outcome: Architecture gap identified; effect of any subsequent change is unmeasured.
transfer_test: Persist the same lesson from independently repeated observations, restart and replay, compare against no-memory and placebo arms.
limitations: Different systems support different goals; no numerical relative performance measured.

title: A learned Breakout policy reproduced on a second training randomization
observation: After 3,000 training games per run, original selected checkpoint averaged 11.305 bricks versus 1.355 cold over 200 holdout games; fresh training RNG and disjoint game seeds averaged 12.040 versus 1.360 cold. Windows and Linux verified identical hash-linked two-run receipts.
how_learned: Researcher-instrumented SpongeTD Q-learning updated tabular reward values in a simplified Breakout environment; separately seeded validation chose checkpoints and unexposed holdouts measured outcomes.
what_changed: Committed an append-only SHA-linked research scoreboard and published separate original-versus-new-seed metrics on BEAN Pages; research policy remains isolated from Core Main.
actual_learning_mechanism: tabular temporal-difference Q-learning policy value updates with journal-backed restart recovery
validated_outcome: Game-specific trained policies outperformed cold baseline across two train-seed protocols; OS reproduction is deterministic, not extra independent training. No proof of outperforming conventional Q-learning or learning algorithm self-improvement.
transfer_test: Repeat across many preregistered training seeds, unseen game rules and distinct environments with frozen baselines, matched classical Q-learning comparator, uncertainty intervals, and blinded independent evaluators.
limitations: Simplified synthetic Breakout; two randomizations in one environment; checkpoint selection used validation; hashes verify bytes, not truth; no BEAN higher-level cognitive transfer demonstrated.
